I feel like I should contribute to the discussion here, although pointing out problems with this article is like telling a tall tree that it grew wrong.

Notes
– hide block
  • The Foundation is not being its usual, careful self here when it:
    • Regards SCP-A instances as hostile, and without any supplied reasoning.
    • Shoots SCP-A instances in order to keep them from escaping the pit when a less-radical method (e.g. a barrier added to the top) would do fine.
    • Regards the information obtained from the -B instance of Researcher Patton as credible, without any supplied reasoning; enough so to downgrade it from Keter to Safe, too.
    • Heeds advice that freeing SCP-A instances from the pit "would not be wise", without any supplied reasoning or source.
  • It appears as though the image that is supposed to be in the divs no longer exists.
  • Several of the divs exceed the margins of the rest of the page on (my) mobile.

Hope this helps.

P.S. I'm surprised that so much of the discussion is about the avatar insert.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Reread this in a less-tired state this morning, and I now feel comfortable giving the upvote. I'm usually unsympathetic to concerns of out-of-universe context when judging an article, however I'm increasingly of the mind that if possible, a dedicated rewrite should preserve something of the spirit of the original article. Otherwise just delete the fucker and fill the slot with something else entirely.

LurkD's SCP-466 is a good example of a rewrite that's an improvement while still maintaining the soul of the piece. This article is another, I feel. The seed concept, which is the horror of something else running around as you, is preserved, while taking the initial idea and going much further with it and thereby making this slot a viable article once more. This is some good old-fashioned legitimate creep.

As for the SS references, I've rolled my eyes several times throughout the course of this thread. As someone who loathes the old wacky "let's ride 682 and kill people for no raisin" horseshit, let me tell you that the problems with that era were not the names. It was the fact that you had people who acted like cartoon characters regularly showing up in skips and tales, doing stupid shit and goading each other into ever greater feats of ridiculousness. I'm actually a huge proponent of name-checking SSAA in a tasteful manner as a means of preserving some of the site's history (as opposed to say, decomms, hrrrm ahem etc.), which is important to a lot of people if not myself, without reviving the Bad Old Days of Senior Staff fuckery. Since this is a rewrite attempting to renovate a piece of the old architecture, I say this is a perfectly appropriate place to have Site Director Bright and Dr. Rights. Especially since they either appear as literally only a signature (Bright) or act like actual project managers and scientists (Rights).

You know, a lot of people are saying they aren't very much into the avatar characters, but I rather like them. I mean, I still think Karlyle Aktus is a silly name, but my IRL name gets a lot of dumb comments, too. (Don't ask me to elaborate, because I won't.) I like how Rights got an honorable mention, and honestly like Bright as a character. I don't associate the avatars with the IRL people who created them. Bright the author is not Bright the character, Aktus probably doesn't host a podcast like kaktus, and I don't know anything about Rights the person or much about the character, but I'm sure I could appreciate both.

Quite frankly, I wish there were more good self-inserts around here. I'm sure some people on this site could make good fictional characters by drawing on their own personal flaws, merits, and general personality. Self-inserts on this site don't all have to be lolFoundation and SCP-10101-J, and we as an audience don't all have to have a knee-jerk reaction where we downvote upon seeing someone's username adapted for serious use in a skip. I know a few well-known writers IRL use self-inserts to help fill out the cast of their stories. Why can't we use honest interpretations of ourselves to help populate the fictional world we've built?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is probably going to sound like a dumb reason for not digging something, but here goes:

+ show block
– hide block

First off, it's a vast improvement over the original. I like the world-building in the first and especially the second addendum. (I'm generally in favor of the recent trend of using image/formatting-heavy "realistic" documents to do chronological world-building.)

I also actually like the use of AAs, especially if it pins them to the 70's/80's, which was my impression. That's just fun to imagine.

My other comment is that the central idea here reminds me a lot of SCP-1719, only further developed and with additional story elements added. (A lot of the tropes are also very familiar: missing/deformed facial features, people being replaced and unable to communicate, people crawling out of flesh pits, SCP 5th columns, the fakeout/reclassification tango TL333s was mentioning. The implementation is good, but I think you're reaching for a very comfortable shelf.)

The reason I bring up 1719 is that the exact nature or motivations of those affected were left pretty much blank. This was perfect for a short article with very limited background, and packed a pretty good punch.

In comparison, I think your article goes too far to leave the -Bs as vague as you do. You do the initial world-building with the site details and Foundation blunders. That was well done. Then you mention the interview with Patton-B, but don't print any part of it. The third addendum, unless I'm missing something (which is entirely possible), doesn't really answer any of my questions either.

It feels like you've intentionally painted a box around a big fat question mark. I know that is the very essence of much of SCP, but in this instance, it just left me unsatisfied. No vote for now.
